industry.headline: Federal appeals court upholds Florida's under-14 social media account ban
industry.summary: 11th Circuit reversed a lower-court injunction, finding Florida's under-14 social media account ban (with parental consent required for 14-15 year olds) likely constitutional because it targets platforms with addictive, algorithm-driven features rather than speech itself. Strongest U.S. appellate win yet for state-level youth social media restrictions, validating the 'addictive algorithm' framing central to NOMO's pitch as it pushes US GTM now.

industry.headline: 11th Circuit allows Georgia to enforce social media age-verification law
industry.summary: A second 11th Circuit ruling within 24 hours lifted an injunction blocking Georgia's social media age-verification law, finding NetChoice unlikely to prevail. Back-to-back circuit losses for NetChoice signal a judicial shift toward upholding state restrictions, strengthening the policy tailwind NOMO can cite with US schools and brand partners.

industry.headline: Child advocates oppose blanket social media bans, push for platform accountability instead
industry.summary: Child protection and mental-health advocates publicly opposed outright minor social media bans, instead urging platform accountability, expanded mental-health services, and early intervention. Directly validates NOMO's incentive-based, non-ban positioning as the more palatable alternative for schools and policymakers in the US/UK/AU markets NOMO is prioritizing.

industry.headline: Greece tables bill setting minimum social media age at 15 with mandatory age assurance
industry.summary: Greece's bill, expected to pass by end of October and take effect January 2027, would set a minimum age of 15 for social media with mandatory age verification. Adds another European jurisdiction to the restriction wave alongside the UK, where NOMO's CEO is actively shaping policy.
